title: Priority-driven embedding windowing and region-aware failover for ranker service
creator: Maya Chen
description: Improve the reranking endpoint so it maintains high-quality ordering while scaling to burst workloads and surviving regional outages. This ticket implements a combined approach: (1) priority-driven admission control to prefer tenant-critical queries, (2) embedding-windowing to reduce KV cache churn on long-tail context lengths, and (3) region-aware failover that prefers intra-region degraded variants before cross-region fallbacks. Goal: reduce P99 latency spikes during bursts by 30% and keep quality regression < 1% measured on production eval sets.
acceptance_criteria: Priority queueing implemented that accepts three priority tiers (P0/P1/P2) and enforces admission when queue depth > threshold
Embedding windowing logic reduces effective KV cache footprint for >512-context requests without altering top-10 rerank recall by more than 1% on baseline eval set
Region-aware failover routes to same-region degraded model variant (quantized or smaller head) before cross-region routing; observable in routing logs
End-to-end P99 tail latency for rerank endpoint reduced by >=30% under synthetic burst workload (1k QPS spike) compared to baseline
Automated integration test exercising admission control, windowing, and failover exists in CI and is green
Runbook updated with rollback steps and per-region mitigation knobs
notes: Trade-offs: aggressive windowing helps latency and cache hit-rate but can marginally affect rerank signals for long contexts; mitigated by tier-aware policies that avoid windowing for P0 requests
Decision: use token-windowing at KV-cache insertion time instead of truncation at model input to preserve prefix cache for subsequent requests
Fallback variants: establish two degraded variants per model - quantized (4-bit) and reduced-head (smaller cross-attention head) - chosen via offline eval with quality thresholds
Admission control thresholds initially tuned from production telemetry against 99th-percentile sequence length distributions
